_note: APPROXIMATE program parameters for demo purposes, summarized from public program descriptions. Award ranges and match rules change each funding round; verify against current NOFOs before use.

programs.name: Federal-State Partnership for Intercity Passenger Rail (National)
programs.notes: Primary federal capital program for intercity passenger rail outside the Northeast Corridor main line. Projects in the Corridor ID pipeline are prioritized.

programs.name: Federal-State Partnership for Intercity Passenger Rail (Northeast Corridor)
programs.notes: Limited to projects on the Northeast Corridor (Washington-Boston main line). Only NEC-adjacent elements, such as New York Penn Station approaches, could qualify.

programs.name: Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI)
programs.notes: Safety, capacity and reliability improvements, including grade crossings, sidings and passenger rail improvements on existing lines.

programs.name: BUILD (formerly RAISE) Grants
programs.notes: Highly competitive surface transportation grants capped at about $25M per award; best suited to discrete components such as a station or grade separation.

programs.name: Railroad Rehabilitation and Improvement Financing (RRIF)
programs.notes: Low-interest direct loans and loan guarantees for up to 100% of eligible costs. Must be repaid, so it fits the non-federal share when a revenue source exists.

programs.name: Corridor Identification and Development Program (Corridor ID)
programs.notes: Planning pipeline for new or improved intercity corridors. Step 1 (scoping) is federally funded at about $500K; later service-development steps need a non-federal share. This is the gateway to FSP-National capital funding.
